text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:
- Slovenian Railway workers on Tuesday start a 10-day strike to push for higher salaries. International trains and most passenger and cargo trains are expected to continue running on schedule.

- Parliamentary speaker Janez Podobnik rejected for the second time a proposal from a group of citizens demanding a referendum on whether Slovenia should ratify the association accord, signed with the EU in June last year.
- Slovenia's foreign minister on Monday visited his Polish counterpart Dariusz Rosati to discuss mutual relations and efforts of both countries to join EU and NATO.
- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek attends a trilateral meeting with his counterparts Romano Prodi from Italy and Gyula Horn from Hungary on Tuesday in Budapest.

- Slovenian tyre producer Sava signed a letter of intent to form two separate joint ventures with American Goodyear Tire and Rubber Co.. Agreements between the two companies are due to be signed by mid-summer.

- Macedonia's parliamentary delegation on Monday visited the Slovenian parliament to discuss economic cooperation. The talks indicated that there were no open political questions between the two states.
- Some 50 Slovenian companies will participate in the 17th international building and reconstruction fair in Sarajevo, starting next week.

- President Milan Kucan on Monday met Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek and parliamentary speaker Janez Podobnik. They underlined the importance of ratifying the EU association treaty for Slovenia's joining EU and NATO as soon as possible.
